full_judgment:
5. The defendant No. 1 contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material averments made in the plaint contending inter alia that the suit reveals no cause of action and it is bad for defect of parties and barred by limitation. The further case of the defendant No. 1, in short, is that A. Wahed Howlader mortgaged the suit land to the predecessor of the plaintiffs. Accordingly, a deed of sale with a deed of re-conveyance got registered. A. Wahed Howlader requested Aziz Mollah to execute the return deed of sale after repayment of the consideration money but Aziz Mollah denied. Thereafter, A. Wahed Howlader filed Miscellaneous Case No. XIII- 3137/M-1005/1972-73 before the C.O (Revenue), Madaripur and Aziz Mollah contested the case by filing written objection. Ultimately, the said case was allowed on 28.02.1974 and Wahed Howlader took over possession of the suit land on 11.04.1974 and sold out the same by a registered deed of sale dated 03.04.1974 being No. 2679. Aziz Mollah instituted Title Suit No. 324 of 1974 before the 1a Court of Munsif Adalat, Madaripur and the said suit was dismissed. The defendant No. 1 has been enjoying the possession of the suit land by paying rents after getting his name mutated. The suit land was recorded in the present survey in the name of the defendant No. 1. Hence, the suit instituted by the plaintiffs is liable to be dismissed with cost. 

 10. Mr. Mesbahul Islam (Asif), the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that the judgment and decree passed by the appellate court is not a proper judgment of reversal in accordance with the provisions as laid down under Order 41 Rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure as the learned Judge of the trial court rightly and properly decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiffs with the findings that the suit is not barred by limitation as the defendant No. 1 fraudulently obtained the orders and deeds in question; that the deed of sale as well as deed of re- conveyance dated 11.02.1965 in question for 7 years expired on 11.02.1972 long before the promulgation of Section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 dated 03.08.1972 under P.O. 44 of 1972 which is not applicable in the present suit; that A. Wahed Howlader had no saleable interest in the suit land after the said 11.02.1972 for which the deed dated 03.04.1974 being No. 2679 is inoperative and he had no possession of the suit land on 11.04.1974. The appellate court without adverting the aforesaid findings of the trial court improperly reversed the same and thereby committed an error of law which occasioned a failure of justice. 

 12. He next submits that the plaintiff-respondent-petitioners had been able to prove their case by adducing oral and documentary evidence before the trial court but the defendant could not prove his case stating in the written statement by adducing oral and documentary evidence that he has any possession in the suit land. Thus, the trial court on considering the evidence of the respective parties and the facts and circumstances of the case and also the relevant provision of law rightly and properly decreed the suit of the plaintiff but the appellate court without proper perusal of the evidence on record and on misreading the evidence on record, misconstrued the fact and thereby arrived at a wrong decision by setting aside the judgment and decree passed by the trial court which occasioned a failure of justice. Thus, he prayed for set-aside the judgment and decree passed by the appellate court. 

 16. While deciding the issues, trial court examined 3 P.Ws and 4 D.Ws. The trial court at first discussed the issue No. 3 and found that though the defendant in his written statement stated that the suit is barred by defect of parties but he did not specifically mentioned the names of the respective persons and also at the time of cross-examination there is no such allegation made out by the defendant as such the trial court decided that the suit is not barred by defect of parties. 

 17. The trial court next discussed the issue No. 2 and found that the defendant side in their written statement stated that the grand-father of the plaintiff Abdul Aziz Mollah being aware of the Miscellaneous Case. Thus, the plaintiffs have no locus standi to file the suit after long laps of time but the plaintiff’s side claimed that they had no knowledge about the aforesaid Miscellaneous Case and the title suit mentioned by the defendant. The plaintiffs claim is that they Caine to know about the deed in question on 06.01.2005, when the defendant denied the title of the plaintiffs in the suit land. 

 22. The trial court also considered the P.O. 49 of 1972 promulgated on 03.08.1972 and the provision of Section 95(Ka) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and also considered the decisions in the case of Bangladesh vs. Haji Abdul Gani Biswas and others report in 32 DLR(AD) 233 and found that the decision is applicable in the facts and circumstances of the present suit and deed No. 673 dated 11.02.1972 became out and out a sale deed and after the expiry of the aforesaid deed dated 11.02.1972, the predecessor of the alleged defendant had no right and title in the suit land and the subsequent order passed by the Revenue Officer vide CO. Revenue Officer Miscellaneous Case No. 1005/1972-73 is illegal and the subsequent deed on the basis of the aforesaid Miscellaneous Case vide deed dated 03.04.1974 on the basis of the aforesaid Revenue Case is also illegal and ineffective and the defendant No. 1 has got no right, title and interest by the aforesaid deed. 

 27. The appellate court also discussed the claim and counter claim of the respective parties. The appellate court also considered the certified copy of the order sheet of exhibit-Kha from which it appears that Abdul Wahed Howlader filed redemption case on 29.06.1973 under section 95(A) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. The opposite party appeared on 26.11.1973 and prayed for time. On the next date on 06.12.1973 written statement was submitted on behalf of the opposite parties. Thereafter on 28.02.1972 redemption case was allowed. From exhibit-Kha-2, the appellate court found that Shahjahan Molla son of Abdul Aziz Molla filed a review case on 12.04.1974. 

 31. The appellate court also disbelieved the full contention of the plaintiff witnesses and found that the defendant No. 1 is in possession of the suit land. The appellate court also considered the provision of Section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and the decision referred to by the plaintiff-appellant reported in 32 DLR (AD) 233 and also considered the decision reported in 34 DLR 237 wherein transaction passed and closed principle was set-aside. 

 41. The learned Advocate for the petitioners also referred to some decisions in the case of Mahadeb Chandra Mondal and another vs. Dulal Chandra Mondal and other reported in 25 BLD (AD) 233 wherein it is held, "State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950-Section 95A-As the date of re-conveyance expired before the President's Order No. 88 of 1972 came into force, the transaction in question could not be treated as a usufructuary mortgage transaction and the appellant was no entitle to get back the case land on the basis of Section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act." 

 42. In the case of Abdus Salam Sheikh and others vs. Puspa Rani Shil and others reported in 16 BLD (AD) 299 wherein it is held, "State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950-Section 95A-The clear legislative intent of Section 95A is that cases of sale attended with agreement for re- conveyance whether registered or unregistered would come within the ambit of complete usufructuary mortgage for a period of 7 years and provisions of section 95(4) (5) would apply to such transfer. A contrary view would apply to such transfer. A contrary view would clearly make the provision of Section 95A nugatory and frustrate its purpose."
